repository_purpose: Agent-shareable context bundle for Ryan Lopopolo's harness-engineering work, with explicit authorship and visibility boundaries.

license.scope: Original repository material, Ryan Lopopolo social-post text, and Ryan-authored hyperbo.la article text, subject to the exclusions and other rights recorded in COPYING.md.

sources.title: ARCHITECTURE.md
sources.notes: Introduces the short, stable repository codemap, architectural invariants, boundaries, and cross-cutting concerns.

sources.title: Artichoke Ruby Architecture
sources.notes: Living architecture document descended from Ryan's 2021 codemap, with capability-shaped interpreter boundaries and an incremental backend migration.

sources.title: Document Artichoke architecture in ARCHITECTURE.md
sources.notes: First Artichoke architecture document. The commit message explicitly cites matklad's ARCHITECTURE.md essay; the document maps layers and core interpreter capabilities.

sources.title: Improve ARCHITECTURE.md
sources.notes: Makes Artichoke's incremental replacement of mruby functions through the Strangler Fig pattern explicit.

sources.title: Remove specific mruby version from ARCHITECTURE.md
sources.notes: Removes a literal mruby version to make the architecture document resilient to dependency changes.

sources.title: Store Mrb in mrb_state userdata
sources.notes: Early state-ownership decision later identified by PR #670 as the origin of the Rc<RefCell<State>> model.

sources.title: Destructure State
sources.notes: Non-compiling 114-file experiment that identified state ownership, FFI movement, API mutability, and extension rewrites as entangled work.

sources.title: Preparatory pull requests linked to Artichoke PR #442
sources.notes: Exactly 50 merged PRs with explicit causal links to #442, covering extracted changes, state components, capability APIs, mutability propagation, defect repair, and removal of direct VM access.

sources.title: Remove Rc wrapper around Artichoke State
sources.notes: Second 111-file integration attempt after 50 preparatory PRs; its timeline preserves a Windows access violation and the architectural debts discovered before the cleaned PR.

sources.title: Fix a use-after-free caused by GC cycles with the State moved out
sources.notes: Explains the GC-triggered use-after-free discovered during integration and introduces an explicit FFI-boundary primitive.

sources.title: Remove Rc wrapper from the State struct in Artichoke interpreter
sources.notes: Merged 110-file ownership refactor with a detailed account of the original decision, preparation stream, remaining cross-cutting work, and new FFI invariants.

sources.title: Fix segfault in Artichoke::close
sources.notes: Fixes an intermittent Windows shutdown segfault introduced by #670 and identifies destructor ordering as the cause.

sources.title: Follow-through after the Artichoke state refactor
sources.notes: Repairs heap-value boxing, FFI coverage, fallibility, and package ownership that remained after #670.

sources.title: Implement symbol table and Symbol core class in Rust
sources.notes: Lands the Rust symbol table whose borrowing requirements exposed the state-modeling limitation behind #442.

sources.title: Artichoke pull requests merged during the state-refactor window
sources.notes: GitHub records 200 merged pull requests in the repository between the opening of #442 and the merge of #670.

sources.title: Parse, don't validate
sources.notes: Typed boundary discipline: convert less-structured input into precise values that preserve knowledge and make invalid states difficult to represent.

sources.title: Harness Engineering - first thoughts
sources.notes: An initial response to Ryan Lopopolo's harness-engineering essay through context, deterministic constraints, LLM review, iterative feedback, and control systems. It precedes George Zhang's cybernetic reading and Böckeler's full guide-and-sensor treatment.

sources.title: Harness Engineering Is Cybernetics
sources.notes: Interprets Ryan Lopopolo's harness-engineering essay through cybernetic feedback, sensor-actuator loops, desired state, and system-specific calibration. It appeared between Birgitta Böckeler's initial memo and full article; the public sources document no direct influence between Zhang and Böckeler.

sources.title: Harness engineering for coding agent users
sources.notes: Published after Ryan Lopopolo's 2026-02-11 harness-engineering essay. Offers guides and sensors as a subsequent alternate framing, with computational and inferential controls.

sources.title: How confessions can keep language models honest
sources.notes: Introduces a separately rewarded self-report channel and evaluates it under deliberately induced model failures. It sharpens the evidentiary limits of MLD without making the two mechanisms equivalent.

sources.title: Training LLMs for Honesty via Confessions
sources.notes: Defines the confession-training and judging method, reports its stress-test results, and documents the limits around confusion, unknown failure dimensions, chain-of-thought visibility, and adversarial robustness.

sources.title: Strangler Fig
sources.notes: Describes gradual legacy modernization by identifying seams and moving behavior into independently deliverable replacement components.

sources.title: Polytoken introduction
sources.notes: Defines Polytoken as a local-first coding-agent daemon that manages providers, tools, and CLI/TUI workflows.

sources.title: Polytoken tool reference
sources.notes: Documents model-dependent edit formats, patch_edit, patch-aware filesystem approvals, and the surrounding tool surface.

sources.title: Ryan Lopopolo's Polytoken implementation observation
sources.notes: Records Ryan's observation that Polytoken directly reuses Codex's open-source apply_patch implementation for OpenAI models. Public Polytoken documentation does not independently verify this implementation detail.

sources.title: Codex apply_patch grammar and instructions
sources.notes: Defines the model-visible patch grammar and editing contract implemented by the open-source Codex agent.

sources.title: Agent Client Protocol introduction and architecture
sources.notes: Standardizes editor-agent communication across local and remote setups with bidirectional permission requests, streaming session updates, and MCP integration.
